summary: Mulia Airport (LII) is a small highland airstrip serving the remote town of Mulia in the central highlands of Papua Province, Indonesia. Surrounded by mountainous jungle terrain at roughly 2,000 meters elevation, it functions as a vital link for local communities, missionaries, and workers supporting nearby mining and infrastructure operations. The challenging weather and rugged landscape make it primarily accessible to small turboprop aircraft.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Mulia Airport?
A: Mulia is primarily served by small regional carriers operating turboprop aircraft, with Susi Air being the most common operator on routes connecting to larger hubs like Wamena and Jayapura.

Q: What type of aircraft can land at Mulia Airport?
A: Only small STOL (Short Take-Off and Landing) aircraft, typically Cessna 208 Caravans and similar turboprops, are able to operate safely on the short highland runway.

Q: Is Mulia Airport safe to fly into?
A: Flights operate safely but are weather-dependent; dense fog and heavy rain in the highlands frequently cause delays or cancellations, especially during the wet season.

Q: Are there any passenger facilities at the airport?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of remote Papua airstrips, with a small terminal building and basic waiting area only.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing apps are not available at Mulia; visitors should arrange ground transport in advance through their guesthouse or a local contact, typically using a 4WD vehicle suited to rough highland roads. The airport sits a short distance from Mulia town center, but surrounding roads can become difficult to navigate during heavy rainfall.
local_tip: Dress in layers regardless of the season—mornings at this elevation can be surprisingly cool around 15°C, while midday sun warms up significantly, and sudden rain showers are common.
